referents.why: 'Who enclosed the sea' is the rhetorical question; the implied subject of 'shut off' is the one who did it, the LORD. He is named in 38:1 but is not among this verse's candidates.
'when it burst forth ... it came forth': the subject of these acts is the sea (masc sing).
referents.category: implied subject in a temporal clause

referents.why: 'it burst forth': the sea, the same subject.

links.why: The infinitive 'burst forth' is nested in the 'when' clause.
links.category: clause nested in a temporal clause

links.why: A self-link. A wayyiqtol continues an earlier clause of the same verse, and this is the first clause of the verse.
'when it burst forth' is the temporal clause of 'shut off the sea': the host cl0 holds it.
